data.name: Enosh
data.gender_notes: Enosh is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, the name Enosh is derived from the Hebrew word ‘enosh’, which means 'man' or 'mortal'. This name is mentioned in the Book of Genesis as a descendant of Adam. In the context of biblical names, Enosh symbolizes the human condition, our mortal nature, and our dependency on God. The name Enosh carries the meaning “Man; mortal; human” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Enosh usually hope their child will grow to embody man; mortal; human and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reminder of our human condition and our dependence on God.
data.etymology: Enosh belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man; mortal; human.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Enosh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: ענוש
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ענוש נגזר מהשורש ע־נ־שׁ, שפירושו 'להיות חלש, רופס, או תמות'. הוא קשור למילה 'אנוש', שפירושה 'אדם' או 'בן אדם'. השם מופיע בתנךך, בספר בראשית, ומתאר את האדם כיצור תמות, חלש ופכיר. השם ענוש משמש להדגיש את מצבו של האדם כיצור מוגבל וכפוף לשמיים.

in_greek.name: Ἐνὼς
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ἐνὼς εἰς τὴν ἑβραϊκὴν παράδοσιν συνδέεται μετά τοῦ οὐσιαστικοῦ 'ἄνθρωπος' ἤ 'ἐνὸς', ὃ σημαίνει 'ἀσθενὴς ἄνθρωπος' ἤ 'θνητός'. Ἐν Ἑβραϊκῷ κειμένῳ τοῦ Γένεσις, ὁ Ἐνὼς συσχετίζεται μετα τῆς θνητότητος καὶ ἀσθένειας τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. Ἡ ὀνοματοδοσία αὐτοῦ διατηρεῖται εἰς τὴν Καινὴν Διαθήκην καὶ συνδέεται μετα τῆς χριστιανικῆς δοξολογίας περί τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης φύσεως.

in_latin.name: Enos
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Enos ex hebraico 'ענוש' (Enosh) derivatur, quod significat 'homo infirmus' vel 'mortalis'. In Scriptura Sacra, Genesis, Enos filius Seth, tertius ab Adam, memoratur. Nomen eius reflectit conditionem humanam ut infirmam et mortalem. In traditione christiana, nomen Enos significat fragilitatem et dependentiam hominis a Deo.

in_english.name: Enosh
in_english.long_meaning: The name Enosh originates from Hebrew 'ענוש' (Enosh), meaning 'weak, frail, or mortal man'. It is derived from the root 'ע־נ־שׁ', which conveys the idea of being weak or dying. Enosh appears in the Bible, in the book of Genesis, as the son of Seth and grandson of Adam. The name symbolizes the fragile and mortal nature of humanity. In Christian tradition, Enosh represents the human condition of weakness and dependence on God. The name carries spiritual significance, reminding believers of their mortality and need for divine guidance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Enosh has a rich cultural heritage in the Jewish tradition, being mentioned in the Hebrew Bible as an ancestor of Noah. It represents the common thread that connects all humans - our mortal, human existence. It reminds us of our origins as the children of Adam and Eve and our continued need to recognize our inherent vulnerability and interconnectedness.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Enosh holds deep spiritual significance in the sense that it calls attention to our fundamental dependence on God for our very existence. It echoes the biblical teaching that human life is a precious gift from God, and that we are called to live our lives in close relationship with Him. The name Enosh can serve as a reminder of our mortal nature and the importance of living a God-centered life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Enosh, meaning "man" or "mortal" in Hebrew, symbolizes the fundamental humanity and transience of every person. It is a reminder of our common origin, our shared limitations, and our mutual dependence on God.

biblical_reference.note: Enosh is mentioned as the son of Seth and grandson of Adam.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Enosh is the name of a son of Seth, mentioned in the Bible in Genesis 5:6. The name Enosh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Enosh continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Enosh in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Enosh, which means "Man; mortal; human". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
